message: Reading chapter. Splitting into teachable units…
Found 5 concepts, 9 misconceptions. Top misconception: "smaller chunks are always more precise".
Picking a world where the concept is the verb, not the vocabulary…
World: "The Oracle of the Old Library". The Oracle is the model, the scrolls are the documents, the satchel is top-k.
Binding concepts to verbs: chunking → tune the cut, top-k → fill the satchel, grounding → interrogate.
Rejected Act II (guessable, 64%). A player can win without touching overlap. Repairing…
Act II rewritten: the gold fact now straddles the cut, so overlap is the only way through.
Re-scored: Act II guessable 31%, concept-necessary. 3 of 5 acts kept for the prototype.
Style locked: candlelit oak, parchment, gold rim light. Painting scene 1/3 — the Scriptorium.
Painting scene 3/3 — the Sanctum of the Blue Flame.
Cast sheet: The Archivist (3 moods), The Oracle (3 moods). Portraits kept on-model via reference images.
Tracing colliders from scene art: 11 blocked rects, 2 interactables, 1 exit per scene.
Walkability check passed: spawn reaches every interactable and exit.
World ready. 3 acts, 3 scenes, 2 characters. Step into the Scriptorium.
